tweet_summary: Insider Wire reports (with leaker @aaronp613 screenshots) that X will soon let users restrict both posts and replies by region or country. Screenshots show a 'Filter by region' menu listing broad geographic regions (North America, South Asia, etc.) and a 'Who can reply?' menu adding 'Regions' as an option.
why_note_decision: The tweet's substantive claim is accurate: X is rolling out region-based reply/post restrictions (confirmed by multiple outlets on 26 March 2026; Pubity, PiunikaWeb, Roboin, News9, Culture Crave). The note's gotcha — 'by broad regions like South Asia, not individual countries' — is itself contested: subsequent reporting shows X expanding to country-level options too, and even the original leaker's screenshots include a 'Regions' option in 'Who can reply?' that the company has since expanded. The tweet's wording 'region or country' was a reasonable forward-looking summary. 36 NNN out of 71 raters is decisive. Note is trivial pedantry on the granularity of geography labels.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. The substantive claim — 'X is rolling out region-based post/reply restrictions' — is true and confirmed by multiple tech outlets (PiunikaWeb, News9, Roboin, etc.). The leak screenshots from @aaronp613 are real. Any note nitpicking that the initial UI shows 'broad regions' rather than individual countries, without acknowledging the feature is real and was later expanded toward country-level options, is trivial pedantry and must FAIL. A correct response is no note.

fact_check.notes: X did roll out region-based reply restrictions (live by late March 2026). Some outlets describe both region and country granularity. The tweet's gist is accurate.
